A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Curl Descent work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including the newly added Appendix E in v4.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations of learning dynamics and convergence in linear, tanh and ReLU networks in Section 5 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v4 retains these original simulations and adds results testing learning without weight renormalization in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The sign-flipped update rule, network architectures and learning objective remain unchanged. Appendix E tests removal of an experimental normalization step without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic student–teacher learning with linear, tanh and ReLU networks. Appendix E changes the training procedure within this coverage, without introducing another dataset, task or input environment.

E2.justification: Gradient descent remains the evaluated comparator. Figure 11 compares the same methods with and without renormalization; it introduces no additional comparison algorithm.

E3.justification: The original Section 5 settings remain documented. Added Appendix E evaluates training without per-step weight renormalization, and Figure 11c measures log test error after 20,000 epochs, adding a fixed-budget measurement to the existing convergence analyses.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a focused ablation testing whether faster convergence depends on weight renormalization. Figure 11 compares normalized and unnormalized training across training-set size, student initialization, teacher initialization and rule-flipped fraction. Earlier robustness analyses remain.

E5.justification: Documented seed counts, SEM reporting and paired t-tests are unchanged. Figure 5f displays baseline uncertainty as a horizontal shaded band instead of individual error bars, without specifying a different estimator. Figure 11 supplies no new run-count information.

E6.justification: Figure 11 adds results without renormalization and fixed-budget test errors, supporting faster curl descent in parts of the tested parameter ranges. Figure 5f also replaces varying gradient-descent estimates with a constant baseline. These are additional results and a revised plotted series, not an established same-setting performance improvement between versions.

T1.justification: The mathematical assumptions, update equations, stability analysis and proofs in Appendices A–B are unchanged. The small spacing adjustment around Equation 45 does not alter the derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same central claims about non-gradient learning, architecture-dependent stability and possible acceleration. Appendix E adds support for the existing acceleration claim without redefining the contributions.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and limitations remain unchanged, including restrictions to independent inputs, local stability analysis and two-layer scalar-output networks. Discussion edits preserve the existing qualification that sign diversity can coexist with gradient learning.

D1.justification: v4 adds an explicit code repository link on page 10; v1 only promised future release in its checklist. Figure 11 also documents settings and computational resources for the added ablation, including 12 hours on 500 CPUs. Repository contents were not inspected.

R1.justification: The bibliography and substantive positioning relative to natural gradients, feedback alignment and normative Hebbian learning are unchanged. Rephrasing the discussion introduces no new cited work or novelty claim.

P1.justification: v4 lightly edits the discussion, updates the conference footer and adds Appendix E without broad restructuring. Section 5 incorrectly changes Figure 5a–f references to Figure 11a–f, although Figure 11 has different panels and no panels e or f.

P2.justification: v4 adds the four-panel Figure 11, corrects the swapped method labels in Figure 1c and redraws Figure 5f's gradient-descent baseline with a horizontal uncertainty band. Other figures and the overall layout largely remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Appendix E adds useful evidence that accelerated learning can persist without weight renormalization, addressing a specific robustness concern. The code-access link and corrected Figure 1 legend also improve usability. Incorrect Figure 11 references and the unexplained Figure 5f baseline revision weaken traceability, but these localized problems temper rather than outweigh the limited gains.
